title: Pardons John Frederick Tate
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to John Frederick Tate as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: On May 24, 2018, President Donald Trump pardoned John Frederick Tate, whose federal case was in the Southern District of Iowa. The Justice Department’s pardon list identifies convictions involving conspiracy, false records, campaign contribution reports, and false statements. It also lists Tate’s earlier sentence: two years’ probation, home confinement, community service, and a $10,000 fine.
description_long: President Donald Trump granted John Frederick Tate a pardon on May 24, 2018. The Justice Department’s clemency list identifies Tate’s case in the Southern District of Iowa and lists convictions for conspiracy to commit an offense against the United States, causing false records, causing false campaign contribution reports, and a false-statements scheme. It records an earlier sentence of two years’ probation, conditioned on six months of home confinement and 160 hours of community service, plus a $10,000 fine. The DOJ table notes that the sentence was amended on October 3, 2016. These details describe the court’s original disposition and the offenses associated with the case; they are not a statement of Trump’s reason for granting the pardon. The list confirms the recipient and clemency action but does not provide an account of how the request was considered or explain which consequences, if any, were affected beyond the pardon itself. The event is therefore a specific presidential clemency grant involving federal campaign-reporting and false-record offenses.
